title: cost-optimization: automate defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
description: This PR implements a coordinated set of changes to automate cost-optimization defaults and tooling: 1) introduce server-side autotune for batching and KV-prefix caching defaults (policy driven), 2) add quantization profile discovery and recommended profiles per model/workload, and 3) extend the unit-economics (uecon) tooling to consume autotune output and generate per-route cost impact reports. Motivation: customers repeatedly request better out-of-the-box batching/caching defaults and clearer guidance on quantization trade-offs. This work reduces manual tuning, improves cost predictability, and enables product metrics for recommendations. Changes include feature flags and an opt-in rollout that defaults to off for Dedicated/Private until telemetry baseline is collected. See linear tasks: ENG-845, ENG-1203. Summary of changes: - autotune service: new controller that samples request traces, computes latency/cost-optimal batch_size and cache TTL defaults, stores policies in config-store; - quant-profiles: scanner that benchmarks quantized variants (int8/4bit per-kernel where supported) and writes recommended profiles to model-registry; - uecon tooling: new CLI and API endpoint that aggregates autotune+quant recommendations into per-route delta reports (tokens/op cost, estimated monthly $ savings). Also includes hooks in Console to show recommended settings in the model route editor. Rollout plan and safety: feature-flagged, canary to 10% of traffic in hosted, disabled for Dedicated by default; we added monitoring dashboards and regression alerts for latency and output-quality.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Left a few nits on controller.go - please factor out computePolicy into a testable helper and add unit tests for edge cases (tiny/huge seq lengths).
Asha Kapoor: addressed in commit 'refactor: extract computePolicy unit tests' - added table-driven tests and a comment about assumptions.
Priya Reddy: Can we add a safety cutoff to avoid recommending >2x batching for low-latency routes? Also request to expose the sampling rate as a config var for Dedicated.
Asha Kapoor: added safety cutoff and sampling-rate config; default sampling is 0.5% for hosted. Documented in docs/engineering/autotune_design.md.
Zoe Chen: Quant scanner looks good; one question - do we persist per-layer quant sensitivity or only whole-model profiles? Suggest storing both when available.
Asha Kapoor: we persist whole-model profile and an optional per-layer sensitivity file. UI surfaces whole-model recommendation by default with a link to advanced per-layer view.
SRE (automated): perf-canary reported a 2.8% median latency delta during baseline run - within alert threshold. Verified on rerun.
Security reviewer (manual): dependency check flagged a dev-only test util; confirmed no runtime risk.
Maintainer (merge): Approved and squashed merge after CI green; merge method: squash and merge.
